text:
Borussia Dortmund’s dreams have a habit of becoming nightmares, like when they somehow handed Bayern Munich the Bundesliga title on the final day of the 2022-23 season. Or when an 89th-minute Arjen Robben goal won the 2013 Champions League final for the same opponents. Whenever Dortmund suffer heartbreak, it usually involves Bayern.
As things stand, however, Niko Kovac’s side hold a two-point lead over Bayern at the top of the Bundesliga. Both teams are unbeaten, but Dortmund may be the more stable of the two at the moment, especially with Harry Kane expected to miss several months through injury.
So can Dortmund make the most of this opportunity to become German champions for the first time since the Jürgen Klopp era? Or is another Dortmund dream destined to end in disappointment?
Will the data catch up with Dortmund?
The table never lies, apparently. The underlying data, however, can call into question the sustainability of a team’s position and, right now, it is casting serious doubt on Dortmund’s Bundesliga title prospects.
Dortmund rank a lowly 13th for expected goals (xG). Seven Bundesliga teams have scored more goals than the leaders, whose lack of open-play creativity is in stark contrast to that of Bayern’s – the Bavarians have scored 30 goals in 10 games and are still underperforming their own xG.
These attacking numbers haven’t been an issue for Dortmund given their defensive strength. Indeed, they are the most resolute defensive unit in the league, keeping more clean sheets than any other side. Having conceded only seven goals from an xG against of 13.4, though, there could be a correction coming.
The difference between Dortmund’s attacking and defensive stats is stark. While Ramy Bensebaini ranks in the top 10 for defensive contributions per 90 minutes this season, Dortmund do not have a single player in the top 30 for chances created. Fabio Silva is their most prolific shot-taker and he’s ranked 27th for shots per 90 minutes. This lack of statistical balance could be an issue over a full season.
Have Bayern’s injuries opened the door?
For Dortmund to win their first Bundesliga title in 15 years, they need Bayern to have an off season. That may be materialising such is the number of injuries the Bundesliga champions are having to handle right now.
Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry and Manuel Neuer have all missed a large portion of the season while Ismael Saibari, Michael Olise and Alphonso Davies have also been absent through injury as Jamal Musiala continues to recover from a neurological condition. Most significant, though, is Kane’s absence. The Ballon d’Or winner, sidelined for a lengthy spell after undergoing surgery on torn ankle ligaments sustained in Bayern’s 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday, has scored an incredible 156 goals in 163 appearances over the last four seasons and is Bayern’s creative heart. Without him, Vincent Kompany’s team simply do not pose the same threat, which was evident in this week’s Champions League loss to Lille.
Dortmund have injury troubles of their own. Giannis Konstantelias is out for the rest of the season after undergoing ACL surgery in September while Emre Can has not played since the spring. Compared to Bayern Munich’s crock list, though, there is not much for Kovac to worry about.
What can Dortmund learn from Leverkusen?
Bayer Leverkusen were the last team to disrupt Bayern Munich’s domestic dominance, winning the 2023-24 Bundesliga title under Xabi Alonso. Just like Dortmund, Leverkusen had a reputation for being perennial bridesmaids – indeed they were nicknamed “Neverkusen” for decades. That season, though, Alonso’s team demolished the rest of the competition, finishing a massive 17 points ahead of the chasing pack on the back of not losing a single game.
Leverkusen did not become nervous down the stretch because they were so far ahead from so early on. There is a lesson in that for Dortmund. They simply must capitalize on any Bayern Munich weakness while they can.
Under Alonso, Leverkusen were relentless. They played with intensity in every match and had an approach that reflected the ideals of their then up-and-coming manager. The Bay Arena was an exciting place to be and that came across in the energy of the team on the pitch. Dortmund have a different sort of energy, but Kovac has instilled a strong set of principles in his players and Dortmund’s form this season is a clear continuation of Kovac’s project. The Westfalenstadion faithful has ever reason to be hopeful once again.
digest_he:
בורוסיה דורטמונד מוצאת את עצמה בעמדת זינוק אידיאלית בבונדסליגה תחת הדרכתו של המאמן ניקו קובאץ', כשהיא מחזיקה ביתרון של שתי נקודות בפסגת הטבלה ומציגה פתיחת עונה ללא הפסדים. היריבה המושבעת, באיירן מינכן, מתמודדת עם מכת פציעות חמורה בסגל, בראשות חסרונו ארוך הטווח של החלוץ המרכזי הארי קיין שעבר ניתוח בקרסול, דבר הפוגע אנושות ביכולת ההתקפית של הבווארים ומעניק לדורטמונד הזדמנות נדירה לזכות באליפות ראשונה מזה 15 שנים.

עם זאת, הנתונים הסטטיסטיים של דורטמונד מעלים שאלות לגבי יכולתה לשמור על קצב זה לאורך כל העונה המלאה. הקבוצה מדורגת במקום ה-13 בלבד בנתוני השערים הצפויים, וסובלת מחוסר יצירתיות במשחק הפתוח, כאשר אין לה אף שחקן המדורג בצמרת ליצירת מצבי הבקעה. מנגד, החוזק המרכזי של דורטמונד טמון בחוליית ההגנה הטובה בליגה, שהצליחה לשמור על רשת נקייה פעמים רבות ולספוג שערים מועטים בלבד הודות למשחק הקרבה והגנה קבוצתית הדוקה.

התרחיש הנוכחי מזכיר את ההצלחה ההיסטורית של באיירן לברקוזן תחת צ'אבי אלונסו, אז ניצלו המרדפים צעדים שגויים של באיירן מינכן כדי לצעוד כל הדרך לצלחת האליפות ללא הפסד. דורטמונד מבינה שעליה לנצל את חולשת היריבה ולשמור על עקביות בכל משחק. האוהדים באצטדיון הבית שוב ממלאים את היציעים בתקוות מחודשות, תקווה שהפעם המסע של קובאץ' וחניכיו לא יסתיים באכזבה אלא בהנפת הצלחת הנכספת.
